title: Terokkar Forest
body: Terokkar Forest spreads across the heart of Outland, a wood of olemba trees between the marshes of Zangarmarsh and the ash of Shadowmoon Valley. It is thought to take its name from Terokk, the mightiest king the arakkoa remember, and his bird-folk still keep their veils in its groves while his city of Skettis waits in the mountains to the southeast. The draenei once held this land. Tuurem was among the first of their cities to fall to the orcs, and their great necropolis of Auchindoun stands in the south. Two years ago a summoning by the Shadow Council tore Auchindoun open, and the blast scoured the forest around it into the Bone Wastes, where the restless dead now wander. Shattrath City rises in the northwest under the Sha'tar. The Alliance holds the Allerian Stronghold and the Horde holds Stonebreaker Hold, and both contend with arakkoa raiders, fel orcs, the blood elves of Firewing Point and the cultists of the Shadow Council.

title: Cenarion Thicket
body: In the forest's north, the Cenarion Thicket was a quiet outpost of the Cenarion Expedition, gathered around a tall tower among the trees. It is a place of the dead now. Something struck it in a blinding white light, and nearly every druid there died at once. Earthbinder Tavgren, away surveying the Bone Wastes at the time, came back to find only one other survivor: Warden Treelos, who still wanders the tower in shifting shapes, babbling of light and silence and of the eyes of Naphthal'ar atop the tower, which will not stop staring. The thicket's teromoths survived as well, but they are vicious now, infused with a residue of pure mana that leaves them agitated and quick to attack.

title: Tuurem
body: Tuurem was a draenei town in the northern reaches of the forest, home to Vindicator Idaar before it became one of the first of his people's cities overrun by the orcs. Its ruins have not been left in peace. Broken of the Wrekt and other scavengers pick through the rubble, and there are rumors of artifact hunters robbing it of relics. Some of its old vessels still brim with raw magical energy, which the high elf Ros'eleth of the Allerian Stronghold hopes will help her scattered people resist the lure of demonic magic. Lately the town has served darker ends: crates of exotic engineering parts bought in Shattrath were delivered here, bound for the blood elves of Firewing Point.

title: Veil Reskk and Veil Shienor
body: Veil Reskk and Veil Shienor are arakkoa colonies in the northern woods, home to Shienor talonites, sorcerers and wing guards. Like every veil of the forest they answer to Skettis. Their warriors ambush hunters and couriers on the roads, strike at the garrisons by night, and escape through summoning circles before a warband can catch them. Each colony guards an Eye of Skettis, an orb enchanted by black art through which Terokk is said to watch over his colonies, and redeemed arakkoa in Shattrath long to look through them. The leaders of the two veils, Ashkaz of Reskk and Ayit of Shienor, are marked for death by the Alliance and the Horde alike.

title: Veil Skith
body: Veil Skith hides in a secluded grove just south of Shattrath, a colony of Skithian windrippers and dreadhawks led by Urdak. The Skithians are bold thieves who made off with a great shipment of exotic goods belonging to the ethereal Wind Trader Lathrai, and they carried children from a refugee caravan back to their cages here. Their altar, the Darkstone of Terokk, was raised for the colony's worship of Skettis, and Kirrik the Awakened hoped a rod blessed by the naaru A'dal could purify it and redeem the Skithians. When the rod was used, the Darkstone exploded, and Kirrik, who felt the blast in his heart, judged that those who would not turn to the Light could not be saved.

title: Stonebreaker Hold
body: Stonebreaker Hold is the Horde's town in the middle of the forest, an orc hold of watchtowers commanded by Rokag. Its people are a mixed lot. The blood elf Advisor Faila wonders what misstep earned her this posting, the troll Tooki warns that the forest holds worse juju than the Alliance, and Kurgatok bickers with his ill-mannered imp. Mawg Grimshot, who lost an eye to the bonelasher king, posts bounties on the beasts, and the trader Rakoria presses olemba seeds into oil to sell along the roads. Messengers run the dangerous road north to Swamprat Post in Zangarmarsh. For Malukaz the hold is something more: a return to a land his people once called home.

title: Allerian Stronghold
body: The Allerian Stronghold is the Alliance's foothold in eastern Terokkar. It bears the name of Alleria Windrunner, and many of its defenders are high elves who stayed in Outland: rangers walk its walls, and the seamstress Ros'eleth admits she once hoped to meet the town's namesake. Captain Auric Sunchaser commands, while Lieutenant Gravelhammer brings him one crisis after another, a burning sentry tower, a missing merchant, mercenaries from Honor Hold stirring up trouble. Trouble rings the garrison on every side. Arakkoa raid its roads, fel orcs dig in at the ruins to the east, and to the south lie the Bone Wastes, where at least one of its defenders flatly refuses to go, whatever the bounty.

title: Firewing Point
body: Firewing Point is a blood elf citadel in the northeast of the forest, its spire rising over a walled courtyard. Its masters serve Kael'thas, and through him Illidan, and its warlocks and bloodwarders guard a terrible project: mana bombs, weapons of pure mana able to wipe out a whole town. The overseer Sharth Voldoun keeps to the top of the highest spire and holds the final codes himself. A Cenarion envoy, Isla Starmane, came here on a diplomatic mission and found herself locked in a cage. On the river's banks to the south and southwest, the Alliance keeps the Allerian Post and the Horde keeps Stonebreaker Camp, small forward posts watching the spire.

title: Bonechewer Ruins
body: East of the Allerian Stronghold lie the Bonechewer Ruins, where fel orcs of the Bonechewer have lately moved in and set to rebuilding. The work never stops: warped peons repair the buildings and raise fortifications day and night, while devastators and backbreakers stand guard and messengers watch the roads. Their arrival troubled both garrisons, for the Horde at Thrallmar had believed the fel orcs safely contained around Hellfire Citadel. The answer lay in plans found in the camp, written in a hand far too delicate for any orc. The Bonechewer take their orders from the blood elves of Firewing Point, who sent a liaison back and forth between the camps, and they were told to keep the garrisons occupied.

title: Grangol'var Village
body: Grangol'var Village is a ruined settlement west of Stonebreaker Hold, on the northern fringe of the Bone Wastes. A shadowy band has moved into its broken buildings: robed summoners and executioners, a laborer who grumbles about his pay, and an advisor who threatens to have strangers beaten. They are the Shadow Council, led by Shadowmaster Grieve, who offers any who cross him a grave in the labyrinth of Auchindoun or a place as a sacrifice to Murmur. Their gossip betrays them, for the cultists whisper that the council has lost all control of Murmur in the Shadow Labyrinth. Scouts from both garrisons keep watch on the village entrances, though their reports went unanswered for more than a week.

title: Bleeding Hollow Ruins
body: On the western border with Nagrand lie the Bleeding Hollow Ruins, until lately a village of Bleeding Hollow orcs. Boulderfist ogres fell on it in a cowardly night attack, and the survivor Jorin Deadeye fled to Garadar to beg for help. The ogres hold the village still. Their fat leader, Unkor the Ruthless, makes his lesser followers dance for him while he waits for something none of them will name, and Kilrath, a scout sent from Garadar, hides at the edge of the ruins, watching. To the Mag'har it is also one of the old villages of their ancestors. What Kilrath and his helpers learned from Unkor is a tale told in Garadar.

title: Refugee Caravan
body: On the road south of Shattrath, at the northern edge of the Bone Wastes, a caravan of refugees from the Lower City sits stalled beside its wagons. Broken and humans, orcs and redeemed arakkoa traveled together until Shadow Council cultists struck in the night, and now their guards wait for the help called from Shattrath. Each traveler has a reason to be here. Kirrik the Awakened seeks his people in the colonies; High Priest Orglum came to cleanse the troubled spirits of the wastes; Soolaveen would ease the pain of the restless dead; Lakotae would heal the blasted land. A boy named Ethan simply wants his friends back, carried off by the bird men in the night.

title: The Bone Wastes
body: The Bone Wastes are a scar of dust and bleached bone at the heart of the forest, left where the blast from Auchindoun blew the land around the necropolis bare. The dead do not rest here. Lost spirits and broken skeletons, draenei corrupted by the explosion, wander in blind torment, and the bones of the fallen lie scattered for any who would carry them to a proper grave. Plague-carrying bonelashers, scorpids and burrowing bone worms prowl the sand, wood mites gnaw at the trees along its edges, and ethereal plunderers and Shadow Council cabalists pick over its tombs. Five spirit towers stand in the wastes, and by ancient custom the living come to pay their respects there at certain hours.

title: The Shadow Tomb and the Tomb of Lights
body: Two tombs lie near the refugee caravan, and neither rests easy. The Shadow Tomb, to the west, has been taken by Shadow Council cabalists fleeing Auchindoun, who use it to store the powerful artifacts they carried out of the necropolis, among them the relics of the patriarchs Arunen, K'alen and Atalor. To the east, buried under charred sand, lies the Tomb of Lights, a lost resting place of the dead. Ethereals plunder its bodies for keepsakes laid beside them centuries ago, and the Shadow Council has corrupted it so deeply that its draenei dead have risen as vengeful spirits, angry and confused, with a burning hatred for the living.

title: Veil Rhaze
body: Veil Rhaze was a particularly wicked colony of Skettis on the western edge of the Bone Wastes, west of the Shadow Tomb. The blast that tore Auchindoun apart destroyed it, but did not end it: the malevolent spirits of its people still haunt the ruins as deathtalons, screeching spirits and spirit ravens, bound to Terokk's will. Overhead circles Torgos, king of the bonelashers, who took Mawg Grimshot's eye while he hunted here. Torgos keeps away from an old arakkoan scarecrow called Torgos's Bane, and hunters say only the carcass of his mate Trachela, laid at its foot, will draw him down. She nests with the other bonelashers at Carrion Hill in the north of the wastes.

title: Veil Lithic
body: Veil Lithic lies in the southwest of the forest, a colony of Lithic oracles and talonguards loyal to Skettis. Its sorcerers practice an especially cruel art. They wrap unhatched eggs in a shadowy curse, so that the hatchlings which emerge are born as mindless servants of Terokk. Kirrik the Awakened of the refugee caravan asks those who would help to break the cursed eggs early, redeeming the hatchlings that can still be saved and putting down the ones the curse has already claimed. Even Kirrik admits it is grim work to meddle with another's hatchlings, but he holds that leaving the evil to brew would be bleaker still.

title: Auchindoun and the Ring of Observance
body: Auchindoun was the great necropolis of the draenei, born from a first tomb where Prophet Velen laid the remains of a fallen naaru, and the Auchenai death priests tended its dead for some five hundred years. Two years ago a Shadow Council summoning tore it open. Its four wings now hold rival powers: ethereals plunder the Mana-Tombs, the maddened Auchenai keep the Crypts, the Sethekk arakkoa hold their halls, and the Shadow Council struggles to contain Murmur, the being it called, in the Shadow Labyrinth. At its center lies the Ring of Observance, where draenei spirits drift among the stones, Lower City agents hold the door of the labyrinth, and the outcast death priest Ramdor grumbles over the bones.

title: The Shadow Stair
body: The Shadow Stair climbs to Auchindoun's northern entrance and the sealed doors of the Mana-Tombs, inside which the ethereal Nexus-Prince Shaffar plunders the crypt for all it is worth. Outside, a rival Consortium camp waits under Nexus-Prince Haramad, who greets visitors by asking those sent to kill him to take a number and wait their turn. His Captain Kaftiz swears that Shaffar's wards will break any minute now, while his artificers look for another way in and a shady dealer sells only to friends of the Consortium. They share the stair uneasily with Shadow Council cabalists, whose skirmishers and spell-weavers gather on its steps.

title: Sha'tari Base Camp
body: Southwest of Auchindoun, the Sha'tar have pitched a base camp in the wastes, where great elekk stand among Commander Ra'vaj's vindicators. Their war is with the Auchenai, and the battle on the Auchenai Grounds east of the camp has raged for days, every fallen soldier on either side snatched away and its soul lifted for some dark rite. The camp is beset on other fronts too: spiders from Netherweb Ridge raided it by night and carried off its people, and Oakun broods over a way to destroy the cursed thing that flies over the wastes. An Explorers' League dig under the hapless Chief Archaeologist Letoll shares the camp, hunting bone worms with a drum unearthed at their dig.

title: Writhing Mound
body: Northeast of Auchindoun, beyond its walls, rises the Writhing Mound, a place where necromancers gather. Auchenai death-speakers and doomsayers work their rites there among rats and restless bones, and the doom skulls they carry are laced with powerful necromantic enchantments. Pale death-spirits linger about the mound. At its heart lies a summoning circle, and the Sha'tar have learned that skulls enough, joined with a relic of true evil, can command Teribus the Cursed to come down from the skies and face whoever called it.

title: Netherweb Ridge
body: On the southeastern edge of the Bone Wastes rises Netherweb Ridge, the lair of the dreadfang widows. The spiders hunt by night, poisoning their victims, wrapping them in webs and carrying them off to the ridge, where cocooned prisoners hang among the rocks. They struck the Sha'tari Base Camp this way, and the warriors who chased them into the dark did not return; Vindicator Haylen and his last companions lie poisoned just west of the ridge. Deep within lurks the brood-mother of them all, the great Terokkarantula, and while she lives the widows will keep on spawning.

title: Veil Shalas
body: At the foot of the cliffs beneath Skettis lies Veil Shalas, the most formidable of Terokk's colonies, home to Shalassi oracles and talonguards. Through Shalas the forward sages of Skettis wage their war on the Light, and four magical signal fires, burning emerald, violet, bloodstone and sapphire, carry word between the colony and its master. One of the redeemed, Skywing, came here hoping to sway the Shalassi toward the Light. They answered with the curse of Luanga the Imprisoner, one of Terokk's most feared agents, which left him a small fluttering bird until a stranger followed him back to Veil Shalas, slew Luanga and saw the curse broken.

title: Blackwind Landing
body: Blackwind Landing is the camp of the Sha'tari Skyguard in the northern Skethyl Mountains, just outside Skettis, where nether rays rest between sorties. The Skyguard is Shattrath's air wing, and after a sharp rise in arakkoa activity was followed by attacks on the city, it posted riders here to watch Skettis from above. The war is hard on them. Dozens of sorties fly each day, feed for the rays runs short, and scouts are knocked from the sky by monstrous kaliri. Sky Commander Adaris lies wounded in camp under the care of Severin, while Sky Sergeant Doryn drills new recruits. Nearby, in a cage, sits an arakkoa prisoner named Hazzik, cursing his captors.

title: Skettis
body: High in the Skethyl Mountains of southeastern Terokkar lies Skettis, the hidden city of the arakkoa, its dwellings rising around the waters of Blackwind Lake. From here Terokk's power reaches every veil in the forest. Its quarters of Veil Harr'ik, Veil Ala'rak and Upper and Lower Veil Shil'ak are guarded by wing guards, windwalkers and soulcallers, and by the strange time-lost arakkoa. Monstrous kaliri, bred as war birds, nest atop the dwellings. On the island of Terokk's Rest at the heart of the city, an old and nearly blind scribe named Sahaak keeps his books, and there, the talonpriests believe, their ancient king will one day return.

title: Earthbinder Tavgren
body: Earthbinder Tavgren of the Cenarion Expedition was away on a survey of the Bone Wastes when death came to the Cenarion Thicket. He returned to find his fellow druids slain and only Warden Treelos alive, his mind broken. Refusing to leave, Tavgren camped outside the thicket and set about learning what had happened, studying mana-soaked teromoths, a dead Broken found with a strange object, and the trail of a merchant's boxes. When the truth came back to him, a blood elf bomb of pure mana, he could only ask why anyone would turn such a weapon on a place of peace and repose, and hope that Treelos's mind might heal in time.

title: Captain Auric Sunchaser
body: Captain Auric Sunchaser is the high elf who commands the Allerian Stronghold and the high elves who chose to stay there. His days are a parade of bad news delivered by his aide, Lieutenant Gravelhammer: a fire in the sentry tower, a missing merchant, a Cenarion druid held captive at Firewing Point. He meets each report with weary questions about what else could possibly go wrong, yet every one ends with an order to see it handled, to call in the scouts or to notify anyone who can help. It is to Sunchaser that the Cenarion envoy Isla Starmane brings her full account of Firewing Point after her escape, and he thanks her rescuers on behalf of the stronghold.

title: Rokag
body: Rokag commands Stonebreaker Hold, and he has little patience for anything that is not defense or supply. When Malukaz chatters about the forest's history, Rokag grants that the work matters but points out that someone must see to the defenses and logistics while the present's problems remain unsettled. His answer to the arakkoa is blunt: kill their leaders in Reskk, Shienor and Skith, and when he hears that some arakkoa in Shattrath claim friendship with the Horde, send a messenger to demand their surrender. He keeps the shadowstalker Kaide watching the fel orcs in the ruins to the east, and is disturbed when their plans reveal that they are colluding with the blood elves.

title: Theloria Shadecloak
body: Theloria Shadecloak is a high elf who watches from the Allerian Post, a small watch north of the Bonechewer Ruins. She is an exile. When the Dark Portal opened she learned what had become of her people, and seeing the Farstriders throw in their lot with Kael'thas ended the homecoming she had dreamed of; her exile spared her their downfall, she says, but this forest is now the only home she has left. It was Theloria who shadowed a blood elf woman from the fel orc camp north toward Firewing Point, and she means to stall any reinforcements the fel orcs try to bring to their ruins.

title: Kirrik the Awakened
body: Kirrik the Awakened is an arakkoa who saw through Terokk. Where others in Skettis took him for a prophet, Kirrik named him a charlatan whose only true prophecy was the doom he brought about himself, and it was Kirrik who bravely led the exiles out of Skettis on their pilgrimage to Shattrath, where they learned of the Light through A'dal. Kirrik did not stay behind the city's walls. He went back out into the colonies in search of others who might be saved, and he now waits with the refugee caravan in the Bone Wastes, guiding strangers against the veils. Those who will not turn to the Light, he has come to believe, are mere servants of evil.

title: Ramdor the Mad
body: Ramdor the Mad stands on the bone pile outside the Auchenai Crypts, scowling at spirits only he and a child can see. He was once a death priest of the Auchenai, a title he now finds unsavory. When Exarch Maladaar turned the priory to experiments in necromancy, Ramdor held that the dead they had cared for some five hundred years should simply be left alone, and he was cast out for his beliefs. He calls the Auchenai insane to the last, yet the dead will not leave him in peace. He is gruff and a self-confessed liar, but he sees that the bones of the ancestors are properly buried.

title: Isfar
body: Isfar is an arakkoa who once followed the Sethekk. When Auchindoun exploded, the Sethekk took it as an omen of their master's arrival and marched out of Skettis with great fanfare to face their god in the temple ruins, and Isfar went with them, for his older brother Syth was one of their leaders. In time he came to doubt Syth and his ally Ikiss, and Syth had him cast out of the halls while keeping their sister Lakka prisoner. Isfar found safety in Shattrath but could not stay. He has crept back to the entrance of the Sethekk Halls, hoping to free Lakka and to restore the stolen relics of Terokk to his people.

title: Sky Commander Adaris
body: Sky Commander Adaris leads the Sha'tari Skyguard at Blackwind Landing, and he leads it from his sickbed. Badly wounded in a Skettis incursion, he drifts in and out of consciousness, muttering that unseen arakkoa are all around, watching and waiting. His healer Severin took it for fevered delirium when Adaris demanded an elixir of arakkoa shadow dust to see into a world of shadows, but the commander was right, for the talonpriests at the head of Skettis had hidden there all along. Adaris is stubborn and slow to trust strange plans, fearing a mutiny among his weary riders, yet once persuaded he commits them fully.

title: David Wayne
body: David Wayne is a human blacksmith who lives alone at Wayne's Refuge, a scrap of land just east of Firewing Point. He came to Draenor with the Sons of Lothar, and though he left Honor Hold behind, he says the Sons never quite leave a man. He cannot fully explain why he went. He only feels that he is not meant to be at Honor Hold right now, and that he may be meant to be part of something larger. His skill at the forge is known well enough that the smiths of Shadowmoon Valley, Alliance and Horde alike, send him work too difficult for their own anvils.

title: Teribus the Cursed
body: Teribus the Cursed is a creature that flies over the Bone Wastes, and Oakun of the Sha'tar means to see it brought down. The key, Oakun believes, is a Dread Relic. Long ago a caravan went to Auchindoun to take it from the ancient tombs beneath the necropolis, and though they fled with it, the relic was their undoing, for it summons evil to whoever touches it; their wagons still lie wrecked to the east. Carried to the summoning circle of the Writhing Mound and joined with doom skulls taken from the Auchenai necromancers there, the relic can force Teribus to come down and fight, and so purge a great evil from the skies of Terokkar.

title: Terokk
body: Terokk is the mightiest and most terrible king in arakkoa history, a hero whose deeds and splendid plumage are still described to every hatchling. He dwelt among his people for hundreds of years and then vanished, leaving behind only his mask, his spear and his writings, relics the Sethekk later bore away from Skettis. Not all remember him fondly. To the exiles of Shattrath he was a charlatan, and the lowest caste of his city would have been sacrificed to the dark powers his talonpriests worshipped. The talonpriests have not forgotten him. Their almanac foretells his return, and when called back too early he rages that the stars are not aligned and boasts that he cannot be killed.

title: The Mana Bomb
body: When word stopped coming from the Cenarion Thicket, the Cenarion Refuge, Stonebreaker Hold and the Allerian Stronghold each sent someone to look. They found Earthbinder Tavgren alone outside a thicket of the dead. Its teromoths were soaked in pure mana, and beside a dead Broken lay a strange object. The Broken merchant Empoor, once beaten into talking, admitted only that he carried boxes for an ethereal in Shattrath. Wind Trader Lathrai's memory improved when his stolen goods were won back from Veil Skith: he had sold exotic engineering parts, delivered to Tuurem. A last box, found there as a blood elf prepared to carry it to Firewing Point, held bomb parts. From forward posts by the river the garrisons struck at Firewing Point, where Sharth Voldoun boasted to his master that the prototype tested on the thicket had worked and a second bomb would soon fall on the nearby pests. Taking his final code, the attackers set that bomb off in Firewing's own courtyard, and both garrisons celebrated their deliverance.

title: The Fel Orcs of the Bonechewer Ruins
body: Fel orcs had come to the ruins east of the garrisons and were building day and night. For the Alliance, Bertelm sent volunteers against their peons and on to Theloria Shadecloak at the Allerian Post; for the Horde, Kurgatok sent them against the same peons and on to Shadowstalker Kaide, watching from the trees. Thrallmar had believed the fel orcs safely contained around Hellfire Citadel. Both watchers had seen a blood elf woman come and go from the fel orc camp, giving orders, then return north to Firewing Point. The liaison, Lisaile Fireweaver, was hunted down, and plans found in the camp, written in a hand too delicate for any orc, showed that the Bonechewer were there to serve the blood elves and to keep the garrisons occupied. Thinning their ranks bought time. Kaide asked one thing more of his Horde helpers: that word of the trouble never reach Thrallmar, lest the hold receive a great deal of unwanted company. Some stories, he said, are best left where they happened.

title: The Shadow Council at Grangol'var
body: A shadowy band had moved into the ruins of Grangol'var Village, and the scouts who spotted it, Private Weeks for the Alliance and Scout Neftis for the Horde, waited more than a week for anyone to answer their reports. When help finally arrived, each scout handed over a flimsy disguise and sent the newcomer in to mingle. An initiate complained that the interruption meant starting his work over, a laborer grumbled about his pay, and a haughty advisor threatened to have the stranger beaten, but between them the truth came out: these were the Shadow Council. The scouts were aghast. Back went the intruders, weapons drawn, to cut down executioners and summoners and their leader, Shadowmaster Grieve, who had promised his enemies burial in the labyrinth of Auchindoun or sacrifice to Murmur. Lieutenant Gravelhammer and Advisor Faila agreed that a Shadow Council stronghold on their doorstep was the last thing either garrison needed.

title: The Wolf Spirit
body: Malukaz of Stonebreaker Hold came to Terokkar through Nagrand, and found to his joy that not all of his people's old ways were lost. Generations ago, he says, when orc clans still called this forest home, the wolf spirit had a place in their lives. When the orcs departed they left it behind, and in time it grew lonely and left the forest too. Malukaz meant to call it home. For his ritual vestments he needed the pelts of the forest's timber worgs, and for the final piece the pelt of Ironjaw, the old and cunning patriarch of the wolves who roams the northeast. With incense made in the days of the clans burning by the runestone in his hut, he called to the spirit: his people had given themselves to evil and forgotten it, but now they had returned to honor it again. The wolf spirit answered, and Malukaz declared that Thrall would be proud. Perhaps, he mused, the spirit had been waiting all along for the orcs to see what their choices had wrought.

title: The Eyes of Skettis
body: Weary of arakkoa raids, Rokag of Stonebreaker Hold sent a messenger to Shattrath to demand the surrender of Rilak the Redeemed, leader of the arakkoa there; Lady Dena Kennedy of the Allerian Stronghold sent hers to learn their secrets instead. Rilak welcomed the curious and told the angry he could do little: some arakkoa had been touched by the naaru and were forever changed, but those in the wild remained as they had always been. He asked for the Eyes of Skettis, orbs through which Terokk watches Veil Reskk and Veil Shienor, and what they showed sent a missive south to Kirrik the Awakened at the refugee caravan. Kirrik began a campaign against Terokk's colonies: the Darkstone of Veil Skith, which could not be purified, the vengeful spirits of Veil Rhaze, the cursed eggs of Veil Lithic and the signal fires of Veil Shalas. Such blows could not go unanswered. Skettis struck back at Shattrath itself, and its attackers were held off only by those who answered the call to defend the city.

title: The Book of the Dead
body: Outside the Auchenai Crypts a draenei child, Ha'lei, sees the dead all around him, and only the outcast death priest Ramdor believes him, because Ramdor sees them too. Wanting the spirits to leave him be, Ramdor promised treasure to anyone who would fetch the book of the dead from Ezekiel, an Aldor of Shattrath. Ezekiel had lied; the book had been stolen. Ruffians of the Lower City admitted selling it to two draenei, the younger of whom kept talking of his master's grand design. The trail led to Nitrin the Learned in Nagrand, and back again to his son Levixus, who now stood atop the ruins of Auchindoun, calling the dead by name and binding them to his will. Nitrin's tincture, the initiation rite of Auchindoun's death priests, opened the stranger's eyes to the world of the dead forever. Levixus fell, and the book went to Ramdor, who confessed he had never known of any treasure. Pointing to the spirits now visible all around, he welcomed his visitor to the fold.

title: Refugees of the Bone Wastes
body: The refugee caravan out of the Lower City had stopped in the northern Bone Wastes when Shadow Council cultists fell on it. Its guards believe the danger has passed. The Broken refugee Mekeda does not, and asked for the cultists gathered at Auchindoun's northern entrance to be driven off before they returned to slit throats in the dark. All Broken were once draenei, Mekeda says, and the spirits of the ancestors dwell in Auchindoun. Orders taken from the cabal, written in a simple shadow cypher learned among the outcasts of the Lower City, revealed that part of the Shadow Council was fleeing the necropolis and hiding powerful artifacts in the Shadow Tomb to the west. Among them were the relics of three patriarchs, Arunen, K'alen and Atalor, which Mekeda would not allow to serve dark ends. A captive of the cultists, Mekeda's friend Akuno, was brought back to the caravan alive. The Light might have forgotten Mekeda, the refugee says, but Mekeda has not forgotten the Light.

title: The Fallen Exarch
body: In the Bone Wastes the vindicators of the Sha'tar under Commander Ra'vaj have battled the Auchenai for days on the grounds east of their camp, with no end in sight. Worse than the losses is what follows them. Every body that falls, Auchenai or Sha'tar, is snatched from the field and its soul lifted away. Ra'vaj would not let the fiends feed their rituals on his dead. With proper burial out of the question, he handed out torches to burn every corpse on the field, though he knew it was not enough. A hero was needed. Strikes on the Auchenai initiates and doomsayers kept them busy while his scouts slipped behind their lines, and what the scouts found was worse still: the Auchenai had dragged a coffin out of the Auchenai Crypts and were feeding it stolen souls, and the scouts believed it held the first exarch of the crypts, whom the Auchenai meant to raise. The coffin's contents were destroyed before they could be revived, setting the Auchenai back by weeks.

title: The Skyguard over Skettis
body: The Sha'tari Skyguard welcomes recruits who can fly, but first it wants to see whether they can fight. Those who prove themselves in Shattrath are sent on with a package of explosives to Sky Sergeant Doryn at Blackwind Landing, the camp outside Skettis. There the work begins at once. The arakkoa are breeding monstrous kaliri to use against the Skyguard's scouts, and recruits must blast the hatcheries atop the city's dwellings while dodging the great birds that guard them. Scouts shot down over the city must be led out on foot, and the hungry nether rays taken to the woods to hunt warp chasers. All the while the wounded Sky Commander Adaris raved that the true masters of Skettis were hidden from sight. His healer Severin humored him with an elixir brewed from arakkoa shadow dust, and it revealed a world of shadows where the three talonpriests of Skettis, Ishaal, Skizzik and Zellek, had hidden all along. In Veil Ala'rak, near Blackwind Lake, the talonpriests were found and slain.

title: The Return of Terokk
body: Talonpriest Ishaal carried an almanac of celestial charts in an ancient arakkoa script, and the failing Adaris sent it to Rilak the Redeemed in Shattrath. Rilak read in it the coming return of Terokk, the most terrible king in arakkoa history, and saw only one chance: to bring him into the world before he regained his full strength. Adaris would not hear of it. But Hazzik, his caged arakkoa prisoner, born to the lowest caste that Terokk's talonpriests once sacrificed, quietly offered a bargain. In one of the shabby disguises he used to make for ethereal book smugglers, a stranger fooled the nearly blind scribe Sahaak at Terokk's Rest into handing over the Adversarial Bloodlines, which named the descendants of Terokk's ancient enemies, held captive by the talonpriests. Prophecy said their deaths would herald his return. Gezzarak the Huntress, the crystal giant Karrog, the heretic Darkscreecher Akkarai and Vakkiz the Windrager were summoned and slain. At last Adaris relented and sent his riders. Called to Terokk's Rest before the stars aligned, Terokk fell.
